description: A proactive 4-2-3-1 using a double pivot behind three attacking midfielders and one striker.
whyGood: The pivot stabilises build-up while the front four occupy several attacking lines.
whyThisShape: A 4-2-3-1 with a double pivot behind three attacking midfielders and one striker. One of the pivot wins the ball and the other passes it, and the front four occupy several lines of attack.
whenToUse: As a proactive default when you have a good attacking midfielder and two quality wide attackers, or against opponents who defend with two banks of four.
whenNotToUse: When you have no ball-winner to pair with a playmaker, or against a team with three central midfielders who outnumber your pivot.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Keeps possession through the pivot and attacking midfielders.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: The pivot offers short passing options from the defenders.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Moves the ball forward quickly to the front four.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Presses at once after losing the ball, led by the ball-winning midfielder.
instructionRationale.Counter: Attacks quickly when the ball is won, using the runners.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Presses higher up the pitch to keep the play in the opponent's half.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: A balanced line keeps the defence compact.
